- "supported": every factual part of the sentence (each number, each name, each count, each comparison, each cause, each "most", "all", "only" or "none") is stated by one or more of the claims, or follows from them directly with no new number. Give the ids of the claims that together support it.

- "no_factual_content": the sentence states nothing that could be true or false about the world: a transition, a statement of what the section will do, a definition of a word the report uses.

The NAMES table maps a code in a claim to the name a sentence uses; a sentence that uses the name is read as if it used the code. A sentence that names a statistical body is checked against the claims for that body.

SENTENCES
S1: Turning from the measurement's design to its results, the scanner identified itself and carried no credentials, and on 341 of its 1,055 findings it met a denial of access, in which the host answered with an HTTP 401, 403 or 429 status, disallowed the request in robots.txt, or reset the connection.
S2: The remaining outcomes divide into 415 absences, where the thing sought is not served at all, 57 cases where something is served but does not meet the test, 65 other errors, such as failures on the server, responses the scanner could not parse and a redirect loop, and 177 passes.
S3: Three bodies refused the scanner more completely than any other.
S4: At the Bureau of Labor Statistics and at the Office of Research, Evaluation, and Statistics of the Social Security Administration, every one of the 45 findings was a denial, so neither body produced a single absence or a single pass.
S5: The Bureau of Transportation Statistics came close behind, refusing 41 of its 45 and passing only 2.
S6: Bodies with 89 findings each were refused less completely but still often; for example, the Bureau of Economic Analysis turned the scanner away on 40 of them.
S7: At the other end of the range, Statistics of Income at the Internal Revenue Service refused the scanner on only 4 of its 67 findings, and all 4 were robots.txt disallows.
S8: That body was not open in any fuller sense, however, because 44 of the 67 are absences and only 12 pass.
S9: The National Center for Education Statistics and the National Animal Health Monitoring System each refused 10 of 45.
S10: Data.gov is kept apart from these bodies because it is a comparator host and not one of them, and it refused the scanner on 1 of 9 while passing 7.
S11: These denials bear on public access as well as on the scanner, because, as the opening section set out, the public reaches a publisher through AI tools only as far as that publisher's restrictions on crawlers allow.
